meeting.title: ChowNow go-live readiness review
meeting.summary: Go-live readiness review for ChowNow's self-serve rollout. Walked the readiness checklist: SSO (Okta SAML) done and tested, role-based permissions mapped, AI analyst guardrails configured and scoped to the orders mart. Parity is the last open gate — two of the three timezone-cast dashboards now match after the staging fix; the third is being retested. Agreed a provisional go-live date one week out, firmly conditional on Lucia's parity sign-off. Set a rollback plan and a day-one support rota.
action_items: Kevin to finish retesting the third dashboard and report parity numbers by Friday
Lucia to give final parity sign-off, which unblocks the readiness review completion
Caroline to lock the provisional go-live date once parity signs off
Sandra to confirm the day-one support rota and send rollout comms on go-live morning
key_decisions: Provisional go-live set for one week out, conditional on parity sign-off
Rollback plan: keep Tableau read-only for two weeks post-launch as a fallback
AI analyst launches scoped to the orders mart only; wider access is a fast-follow
meeting.notes: Everything green except parity, and parity is on a short leash. The team is disciplined about not going live on an unexplained variance, which is exactly right for a self-serve launch where numbers will be trusted without a human in the loop. Keeping Tableau as a two-week fallback is cheap insurance.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Readiness review. I'll walk the checklist top to bottom and we mark each item green, amber, or blocked. SSO first — Okta SAML is configured and I tested a login this morning. Green.

transcript.speaker: Sandra Kim
transcript.text: Confirmed on our side too — I logged in with a rollout-group account and landed in the right workspace.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Permissions — roles are mapped, ops team gets the self-serve dashboards, finance gets the restricted set. Green. Guardrails — AI analyst is scoped to the orders mart only for launch. Green. That leaves parity.

transcript.speaker: Kevin O'Rourke
transcript.text: Two of the three are matching now after your staging fix. The third I'm retesting — it's the same timezone family, I just want the numbers in front of me before I call it.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: So parity is amber, not blocked — we have a known cause and a fix in flight. I'd set a provisional go-live one week out, hard-conditional on Lucia signing parity. Objections?

transcript.speaker: Lucia Herrera
transcript.text: None. I'll sign the moment Kevin's third dashboard matches. I'm not going to gate a launch on a variance we understand and have fixed.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Then let's talk safety. Rollback plan: we keep Tableau read-only for two weeks after launch. If anything looks wrong, people have a reference and we're not scrambling.

transcript.speaker: Sandra Kim
transcript.text: Sensible. I'll set up a day-one support rota — someone from data and someone from Vector on call for the first day.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Good. So: Kevin retests by Friday, Lucia signs, I lock the date, Sandra sends comms go-live morning. This was a clean review — we're one green checkbox from launch.
